grounded_queries.query: Explain how Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) works, including how retrieved documents are used to support a language model's answer. Base your answer only on the uploaded sources and cite the supporting passages.
grounded_queries.notebooklm_response:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a pre-trained parametric memory (a sequence-to-sequence neural model or LLM) with an external non-parametric memory (a dense vector document index) to produce grounded language outputs.

1. Indexing: Source documents are split into manageable text chunks and transformed into high-dimensional vector embeddings via an encoder, then stored in a vector database.
2. Retrieval: A query encoder transforms the query into a dense vector. A neural retriever such as Dense Passage Retriever (DPR) retrieves the top-k relevant passages using similarity search.
3. Integration and generation: Retrieved text chunks are combined with the query as context for generation.

Retrieved documents provide contextual grounding. RAG-Sequence conditions generation on the same retrieved passage across the sequence, while RAG-Token can marginalize over different retrieved passages for individual tokens. Updating the document index can expand or update accessible knowledge without retraining model parameters.
